name: AIAG Automotive Core Tools (APQP, PPAP, FMEA, MSA, SPC)
structural_summary: Five linked methods used across the automotive supply chain to plan, validate, and control production quality: APQP (product/process quality planning), PPAP (part approval before production), FMEA (failure-mode risk assessment), MSA (measurement system validation), and SPC (ongoing statistical process control). Also referenced in aerospace, defense, and medical device supply chains per industry practice.
license_note: The five core-tool manuals are licensed AIAG publications; this is a structural summary only, not a reproduction.

name: Total Productive Maintenance (TPM)
structural_summary: A maintenance and continuous-improvement framework built around eliminating the 'six big losses' that reduce equipment effectiveness, and around OEE as its core composite metric.
license_note: Widely published methodology; concepts are public, specific published texts are copyrighted works by their respective authors.

name: ISO 9001 — Quality Management Systems
structural_summary: The general-purpose international quality management standard. Clause 10.2 (Nonconformity and Corrective Action) is the structural basis for CAPA-style closure-time tracking used across most manufacturing quality systems, regardless of sub-industry.
license_note: Full standard text is a licensed ISO publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: ISA-95 — Enterprise-Control System Integration
structural_summary: An international standard for integrating enterprise systems (ERP) with control systems (MES/SCADA) — directly relevant to Epic 1's MES connector work, since it defines the standard data model most MES vendors align to.
license_note: Full standard text is a licensed ISA/IEC publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: FDA cGMP — 21 CFR Parts 210 & 211 (Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Drugs)
structural_summary: US FDA's binding manufacturing-quality regulation for pharmaceutical products. Governs batch production records, deviation investigation, and CAPA timeliness — the structural reason pharmaceutical CAPA/audit targets are tighter than general-manufacturing norms (a batch failure can mean destroying the whole batch, not reworking a unit).
license_note: Public US federal regulation (eCFR) — no license restriction, but this is a structural summary, not the regulation's full text.

name: OSHA Process Safety Management (29 CFR 1910.119) + API Recommended Practices
structural_summary: OSHA's process-safety regulation for facilities handling highly hazardous chemicals, paired with API's recommended practices for refining/petrochemical operations. Governs incident investigation, mechanical-integrity audits, and management-of-change — the reason this sub-industry's audit and safety-incident targets carry as much weight as quality KPIs, and why continuous-process uptime (not changeover speed) drives the OEE benchmark.
license_note: OSHA regulation is public domain; API Recommended Practices are licensed API publications — this is a structural summary only, not a reproduction.

name: ISO 10377 — Consumer Product Safety: Guidelines for Suppliers
structural_summary: ISO guidance for consumer-product suppliers on hazard identification, risk assessment, and post-market surveillance (recalls, complaint handling). The structural reason consumer-products Customer Return Rate tolerance is set higher than in B2B/regulated sectors — retail-channel returns are an expected cost of doing business here, not a quality-escape signal on their own; the standard's emphasis is on catching the pattern, not the individual return.
license_note: Full standard text is a licensed ISO publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: ISO 55000 — Asset Management (Overview, Principles, Terminology)
structural_summary: The international standard for managing physical assets over their lifecycle — directly relevant to industrial-products manufacturers' emphasis on planned vs. corrective maintenance ratios and asset uptime, where equipment is typically higher-cost and longer-lived than in high-volume consumer manufacturing.
license_note: Full standard text is a licensed ISO publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: IPC-A-610 — Acceptability of Electronic Assemblies
structural_summary: The electronics-manufacturing industry's standard defining acceptance criteria (Class 1/2/3) for soldering, assembly, and defect classification on populated boards. The structural reason electronics scrap-rate and end-of-line defect-count targets are set in PPM-level terms rather than the broader percentages used elsewhere — component cost and defect classification granularity are both far finer-grained in this sector.
license_note: Full standard (including acceptance-criteria photos) is a licensed IPC publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: Scientific Molding / Decoupled Molding (RJG Inc. Methodology)
structural_summary: A widely-adopted injection-molding process methodology that separates the fill, pack, and hold phases of the molding cycle (using cavity-pressure sensors) so each can be optimized and controlled independently, rather than treating a mold's process settings as one interdependent block. The structural reason this platform's changeover-time and post-changeover scrap/COPQ guidance for this sub-industry emphasizes isolating one process variable at a time rather than a broad multi-parameter adjustment.
license_note: RJG Inc.'s specific training curriculum and certification materials are proprietary; this is a structural summary of the publicly-described methodology principles only, not a reproduction of licensed training content.

name: IATF 16949 — Automotive Quality Management System Requirements
structural_summary: The automotive-specific QMS standard, built on ISO 9001's structure but adding automotive-sector requirements: PPM-level defect tracking, OEM-specific customer requirements (Ford Q1, GM BIQS, Stellantis, etc.), risk-based thinking applied to product safety and regulatory compliance, and mandatory use of the AIAG Core Tools. The structural reason automotive CAPA/8D closure and Cpk thresholds are stricter than the generic ISO 9001 baseline this platform also cites for this sub-industry.
license_note: Full standard text is a licensed IATF publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: IPC J-STD-001 — Requirements for Soldered Electrical and Electronic Assemblies
structural_summary: The companion standard to IPC-A-610: where IPC-A-610 defines what an ACCEPTABLE finished assembly looks like, J-STD-001 defines the soldering PROCESS and materials requirements (flux, alloy, thermal profile qualification) that are supposed to produce that result. The structural reason a reflow-profile-drift root cause (see this sub-industry's solder-defect playbook) is a process-qualification question, not just an inspection-criteria question.
license_note: Full standard is a licensed IPC publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: ASTM D3641 — Standard Practice for Injection Molding Test Specimens of Thermoplastic Molding and Extrusion Materials
structural_summary: A materials-testing practice standard defining how thermoplastic resin specimens should be molded for property testing/qualification — relevant as the structural basis for verifying an incoming resin lot actually matches the material spec a process was originally qualified against, the check called for in this sub-industry's changeover-variation playbook.
license_note: Full standard text is a licensed ASTM publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: API RP 754 — Process Safety Performance Indicators for the Refining and Petrochemical Industries
structural_summary: Defines a four-tier pyramid of process-safety indicators (Tier 1-2 = actual loss-of-containment events, Tier 3-4 = near-misses and leading operating-discipline indicators) — the structural reason this sub-industry's audit/maintenance-alert guidance distinguishes a leading indicator from a lagging one rather than treating all findings on one severity scale (see this sub-industry's leading-vs-lagging playbook).
license_note: Full recommended practice is a licensed API publication; this is a structural summary only.

name: ICH Q7 — Good Manufacturing Practice Guide for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients
structural_summary: The internationally-harmonized GMP guideline specifically for API (drug substance) manufacturing, complementing 21 CFR 211's finished-dose focus. Governs laboratory controls and out-of-specification (OOS) result handling — the structural basis for this sub-industry's OOS investigation playbook, which is a distinct process from a general in-process deviation investigation.
license_note: Published by ICH; widely available without a paywall, but treat as a structural summary, not the guideline's full text.

name: CPSC Regulations — 16 CFR (Consumer Product Safety)
structural_summary: US federal consumer-product-safety regulations (recall authority, reporting requirements under the Consumer Product Safety Act, traceability labeling under 16 CFR Part 1130) — the binding regulatory layer underneath the voluntary ISO 10377 guidance this platform already cites for this sub-industry; ISO 10377 tells you how to run post-market surveillance well, 16 CFR is what makes reporting a genuine hazard pattern mandatory, not optional.
license_note: Public US federal regulation (eCFR) — no license restriction, structural summary only.

name: ISO 55001 — Asset Management: Management Systems Requirements
structural_summary: Where ISO 55000 (already cited for this sub-industry) is the overview/terminology standard, ISO 55001 is the certifiable REQUIREMENTS standard — it specifies what an asset-management system must actually do (risk-based maintenance planning, performance evaluation, continual improvement), which is the structural basis for treating a rising corrective-vs-planned maintenance ratio as a system-conformance gap, not just a scheduling inconvenience.
license_note: Full standard text is a licensed ISO publication; this is a structural summary only.
